paper.title: Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with reward distributions supported in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: a K-armed bandit problem is defined by random variables X_{i,n} for 1 ≤ i ≤ K and n ≥ 1 ... Successive plays of machine i yield rewards X_{i,1}, X_{i,2}, ... which are independent and identically distributed according to an unknown law with unknown expectation µ_i.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with [0,1] rewards, known lower bound d on the gap (epsilon_n-greedy)
settings.definition_quote: if policy εn-GREEDY is run with input parameter 0 < d ≤ min_{i:µi<µ*} Δ_i ... here we need to know a lower bound d on the difference between the reward expectations of the best and the second best machine.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with normally distributed rewards, unknown means and variances
unmapped: Rewards are Gaussian with unknown means and unknown (arm-dependent) variances
settings.definition_quote: the bandit problem with normally distributed rewards ... achieves logarithmic regret uniformly over n without knowing means and variances of the reward distributions.

source.quote: For all K > 1, if policy UCB1 is run on K machines having arbitrary reward distributions P1, ..., PK with support in [0, 1], then its expected regret after any number n of plays is at most 8 \sum_{i:µi<µ*} (ln n)/Δ_i + (1 + π^2/3) \sum_{j=1}^K Δ_j

results.notes: Regret defined via expected pull counts, so pseudo-regret. Paper remarks Theorems 1-3 also hold under weaker assumption E[X_{i,t}|X_{i,1..t-1}] = µ_i and dependence across arms.

symbols.alpha_ucb2: UCB2 input parameter, 0 < alpha < 1, epoch growth tau(r) = ceil((1+alpha)^r)

source.quote: For all K > 1, if policy UCB2 is run with input 0 < α < 1 on K machines having arbitrary reward distributions P1, ..., PK with support in [0, 1], then its expected regret after any number n ≥ max_{i:µi<µ*} 1/(2Δ_i^2) of plays is at most \sum_{i:µi<µ*} ( (1+α)(1+4α) ln(2enΔ_i^2) / (2Δ_i) + c_α/Δ_i )

results.notes: Formula reconstructed from lossy PDF text; proof uses α < 1/10 in a step though theorem states 0 < α < 1.

symbols.d_gap: input lower bound d on the minimal gap, 0 < d <= min_i Delta_i
symbols.c_alg: exploration constant c > 0 of epsilon_n-greedy, eps_n = min{1, cK/(d^2 n)}

source.quote: For all K > 1 and for all reward distributions P1, ..., PK with support in [0, 1], if policy εn-GREEDY is run with input parameter 0 < d ≤ min_{i:µi<µ*} Δ_i, then the probability that after any number n ≥ cK/d of plays εn-GREEDY chooses a suboptimal machine j is at most c/(d^2 n) + 2 (c/d^2) ln((n−1)d^2 e^{1/2}/(cK)) (cK/((n−1)d^2e^{1/2}))^{c/(5d^2)} + (4e/d^2)(cK/((n−1)d^2e^{1/2}))^{c/2}.

results.notes: Bound on probability of playing a given suboptimal arm j at round n (instantaneous). Regime stated as n >= cK/d in theorem, though proof uses n >= cK/d^2. Remark: for c > 5 this is c/(d^2 n) + o(1/n).

conditions: proof relies on Conjectures 1 and 2 (tail bounds for Student and chi^2 distributions) verified only numerically

source.quote: For all K > 1, if policy UCB1-NORMAL is run on K machines having normal reward distributions P1, ..., PK, then its expected regret after any number n of plays is at most 256(log n) \sum_{i:µi<µ*} σ_i^2/Δ_i + (1 + π^2/2 + 8 log n) \sum_{j=1}^K Δ_j

results.notes: Conditional on numerically verified conjectures. Gaussian with unknown variances mapped to subgaussian noise.
